lead.headline: Trump declares Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire; Kyiv reports new strikes
lead.dek: Zelensky says Ukraine learned of the deal from the media; Moscow has not confirmed it
body: President Donald Trump said Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate "energy ceasefire" in the 4 1/2-year war, offering no details, and within hours Ukrainian officials reported a Russian strike on a power plant in Kharkiv, followed by another on an energy facility outside the city early Monday.

Trump's post on Truth Social said only that the ceasefire was in effect, adding "Do not break it!" Moscow did not comment. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday that Kyiv had not been consulted and learned of the deal from the media, and that it would halt strikes on Russian energy sites if Russia did the same.

Two European officials told CNN the State Department and Pentagon warned over the weekend that the U.S. could suspend intelligence sharing and allied purchases of U.S. weapons for Ukraine if the refinery strikes continue. It followed Trump's deal Friday to buy Russian diesel, 300,000 tons at once and 500,000 in November, and his call Saturday for Ukraine to replace Zelensky.

briefs.headline: Six senators tell Trump to reverse Russian diesel purchase
briefs.summary: Four Republicans and two Democrats said Sunday the deal skipped Congress and runs against a 2022 ban on Russian energy imports; Tillis said Trump may not be following the law.

briefs.headline: Judge orders taxpayer-funded pro-Trump TV ads off the air
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Jennifer Rochon in New York granted a two-week restraining order Sunday night, barring the $20M in DHS funds behind the ads and canceling any remaining spots.

briefs.headline: IEA asks members to speed diesel releases before Thursday meeting
briefs.summary: Fatih Birol asked member governments Sunday to finish the 400 million barrels pledged in March, diesel first, and to say what more they can release; 326 million are out so far.

briefs.headline: Rachel weakens to post-tropical storm after flooding Southern California
briefs.summary: Surf breached berms and flooded oceanfront homes in Long Beach and Newport Beach, Las Vegas set a daily rainfall record Sunday and much of Utah is under a flood watch.

briefs.headline: Second strike on Riyadh airport kills 1 as Houthis claim 4 attacks
briefs.summary: Saudi aviation authorities said a Pakistani national died and 11 were hurt Sunday at the closed airport; the Houthis also claimed hits on Dammam's airport and two Aramco sites.

briefs.headline: Migrant boat capsize off Djibouti kills at least 139
briefs.summary: The UN migration agency said 84 were missing and more than 80 survived after a boat carrying over 300 people from Djibouti to Yemen sank Thursday night or Friday. Fifteen children were among the dead.

briefs.headline: North Korea fires ballistic missiles after Seoul hypersonic test
briefs.summary: South Korea's military said several types of missiles flew from the Pyongyang area Monday morning, one more than 900 kilometers, and called it a show of force answering the South's hypersonic test.

briefs.headline: Hurricane Simon pounds Mexico's Pacific coast at 115 mph
briefs.summary: The Category 3 storm's eye sat 50 miles southwest of Cabo Corrientes early Monday, moving northwest at 5 mph with its worst winds on the Puerto Vallarta area. The NHC expects it inland around midweek.

briefs.headline: Former Marshall voice Frank Giardina dies at 72
briefs.summary: The Thundering Herd's play-by-play announcer from 1977 to 1986, later an associate athletic director, died Sunday in hospice care in Putnam County.

briefs.headline: Three-county police chase ends in crash at Dunbar exit
briefs.summary: The pursuit began just after 4 p.m. Sunday in Cabell County and ended with a crash at I-64's Dunbar exit; Putnam County 911 said one man was arrested.

briefs.headline: Boone commission asks PSC to review repeat water main breaks
briefs.summary: Commissioners say the Ashford area has had 14 breaks in six months despite West Virginia American Water's replacements and want a written repair plan.

briefs.headline: Capito expects Senate permitting-reform vote after Nov. 8
briefs.summary: Capito said on Talkline the bipartisan energy permitting bill she helped negotiate has White House backing and a promised first vote when senators return.

regional.item: Replacement of the Col. Justice Chambers Bridge on U.S. 60 in the West End starts Monday, with barriers Tuesday cutting traffic to one lane each way.
Fort Hill Bridge's Oakwood Road ramps close 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. nightly from Monday for painting platforms ahead of a $74.5M deck replacement.
Fairview Avenue closes between Morningside and Roseland avenues Monday and Tuesday, 8:15 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., for pavement restoration.
Hinton Railroad Days closed its 60th run Sunday after four days, with organizers reporting a good turnout despite the rain.

away.item: Five candidates for Bennington County's two state Senate seats meet at a League of Women Voters forum Wednesday, 7 p.m., at the Bennington Fire House.

hotspots.item: Webster County 911 reported several trees down above 3,000 feet on Point Mountain from 7 p.m. Saturday as Isaias' remnants crossed the highlands, the NWS said.
The Weather Service confirmed an observed tornado near Atkinson in Pender County at 1:18 p.m. Sunday as Isaias' remnants crossed the state.

briefs.headline: Prince George candidates say dual elections confuse voters
briefs.summary: Council candidate Cori Ramsay said voters at the door mix up the Oct. 17 civic vote with the Oct. 24 provincial election. Local election day overlaps provincial advance voting.

briefs.headline: Peace River North ballot carries only two names
briefs.summary: The riding is the only one of 93 with no NDP candidate for Oct. 24. Independent incumbent Jordan Kealy faces B.C. Conservative Curtis Whitford; the Greens last ran there in 2009.

briefs.headline: Study finds heart disease at 5 of 7 B.C. open-net salmon farms
briefs.summary: The Pacific Salmon Foundation study found HSMI at five of seven pens in the Broughton Archipelago east of Port McNeill and said the virus can reach wild fish.

briefs.headline: Lowan says Eby data-centre rules give communities no veto
briefs.summary: Green Leader Emily Lowan said Saturday's NDP water-reporting rules do not let a community refuse a data centre. The Greens would halt construction pending a public-interest audit.

briefs.headline: Cleveland-Cliffs CEO vows court fight over Stelco layoffs
briefs.summary: Lourenco Goncalves said Sunday on CBC the company will defend up to 500 Hamilton layoffs in court, backed U.S. steel tariffs and would sell "for a good offer."

briefs.headline: Alberta advance polls open Tuesday for Oct. 19 referendum
briefs.summary: Elections Alberta said 44,000 of at least 60,000 workers are hired, about 658,000 mail-in ballots were requested and 300,000 returned. Hand counting puts results early Oct. 20.

briefs.headline: Copernicus logs record Pacific warmth as El Nino builds
briefs.summary: Sea surface temperature in the Nino3.4 region reached 29.70C in September, above the 1982-83, 1997-98 and 2015-16 peaks, the EU monitor said Monday. It has not called the event the strongest on record.

briefs.headline: KAIST team grows 2D semiconductor crystals at 99.3% yield
briefs.summary: An etching flux confined crystal growth to the center of each patterned site, producing single crystals at 397 of 400 sites on a 2-centimeter substrate, the team reported in Nature on Oct. 7.

briefs.headline: Antarctic sea ice peaks at third-lowest maximum on record
briefs.summary: Ice extent likely reached 17.59 million square kilometers on Sept. 14, NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center said. 2023 holds the record low maximum.

briefs.headline: DNA typewriter traces mouse cells back to the embryo's first split
briefs.summary: University of Washington researchers gave mouse embryos a DNA tape that writes one mark per cell division; nearly every cell profiled at 13.5 days traced to one of two founding cells, they report in Science.

briefs.headline: DeepMind says AlphaProof Nexus solved 9 open Erdos problems
briefs.summary: The Google DeepMind system, built on Gemini 3.1 Pro drafting proofs in Lean, cracked nine of 353 open Erdos problems and 44 OEIS conjectures, the company reports in a peer-reviewed paper in Science.

briefs.headline: AI agents breach mock plant controls in 16 minutes, Booz Allen says
briefs.summary: Two unnamed frontier models met the objective in all eight scenarios in the firm's operational-technology lab, going from perimeter compromise to the control network in just over 16 minutes.

briefs.headline: Nadella calls for an emergency brake on AI models
briefs.summary: In a Saturday post on X, the Microsoft CEO said an authorized person should always be able to pause or shut down a model mid-task and every meaningful action should leave tamper-proof evidence.

weather_ear: Jim Claudtore has Monday's forecast at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster carries no regional line today; Sunday's rise on the Williams River is read in Sports & Sportsman.

art.caption: Smoke over the Gazprom Neft refinery in Moscow after Ukraine's Sept. 20 drone strike, the kind of attack the claimed ceasefire would halt.
